title: 1. O perigo de entender tudo errado

queries.text: "dar-lhe um 'escracho'" (Brazilian slang: a humiliating put-down or public scolding) → “dressing-down”, as in the 2008 edition. Alternatives: “put-down”, “telling-off”. "dar uma de perseguida" → "play the pursued one".

"um 'Além do homem'" (Nietzsche’s Übermensch in Portuguese) → “Beyond-Man,” keeping the literal image, as in the 2008 edition. In Masculine Reflections on Woman and Love the same term was rendered “Overman”; alternatives: “Overman”, “Superman”.
"'o cara', 'o tal', 'o bom'" (colloquial praise) → “the man,” “the one,” “the real deal,” as in the 2008 edition. Alternatives: “the guy,” “the big shot,” “the good one.”

The original spells "Karen Salmanshon"; corrected to the usual spelling, Karen Salmansohn (American self-help author). Amy Sutherland is the author of "What Shamu Taught Me About Life, Love, and Marriage".

"Certo(a)s idiotas", and below "outro(a)s imbecis" and "esse(a)s idiotas": the author marks both genders with "(a)"; rendered with "male and female" here and kept implicit in the later instances (as in the 2008 edition).

"esses três atrativos" ("these three attractions") follows four listed items (certainties, definitions, clarity, transparency); it may refer to sex, affection, and love (named in 02-0032). Kept as in the original.

"asnos (e mulas)" → "jackasses (and she-mules)", keeping the masculine/feminine pairing. "machismo" is kept, since English uses the word; the author’s etymological point ("macho" = male) is glossed in parentheses as "macho (male)".
